A running daemon does not snapshot files beneath a directory whose only .gitignore matches itself (the recording path, not just is_ignored)

unignore_is_honored_without_other_watched_activity: after a mid-run .gitignore edit that re-includes a path, a live daemon records that path with NO other watched activity in the window; the test is RED against the pre-fix daemon

maybe_rebuild_runs_once_per_dirty_flag: maybe_rebuild() returns Some exactly once for a run of consecutive dirty-flag settings and clears the flag, so a hot .gitignore cannot trigger more than one IgnoreSet::build per POLL tick
positive control precedes the ignore-rule edit in the E2E, so the test cannot be satisfied by unrelated watched activity firing the rebuild under pre-fix code

behavior under a stable ignore config is unchanged: self_ignoring_gitignore_dir_is_not_recorded_by_a_real_daemon and records_rich_turn_with_transcript_prompt_and_model_and_filters_ignored pass untouched and un-weakened
the strengthened unit test asserts its own precondition (the edited .gitignore classifies Ignore) so it cannot pass for the wrong reason
daemon_counts_ignore_rebuilds: a live daemon that reloads its ignore set once persists ignore_rebuilds:1 in state.json; a second .gitignore edit makes it 2
status_omits_reload_line_when_never_reloaded: a daemon run with no .gitignore change ends with ignore_rebuilds 0 and bare status prints no reload line at all (never a vacuous '0 reloads')
status_tolerates_state_without_rebuild_counter: a pre-existing state.json lacking the new field parses via serde default and renders as never-reloaded; status --json carries the field
rebuild_count_is_bounded_by_writes: five rapid .gitignore rewrites yield ignore_rebuilds >= 1 and <= 5, asserted on the persisted counter and never by counting stderr lines inside a timing window

SUPERSEDES clm_23B6MYA8 (whose text is false as delivered): the rebuild counter is bounded by POLL ticks, not raw events — 40 rapid .gitignore rewrites yield ignore_rebuilds in 1..=10, and the plan's literal 5-writes/1..=5 form was measured NOT to discriminate its own per-event neuter (5 writes coalesce to ~3 FSEvents notify events)

claim: deleted_gitignore_rewidens_recording: deleting a .gitignore mid-run causes previously-ignored paths to be recorded on their next mutation, with no daemon restart and no unrelated watched activity
new_gitignore_honored_without_restart: a .gitignore created mid-run under a directory that had none takes effect without a daemon restart

nested_gitignore_precedence asserts its own precondition (matchers.len() >= 2) and runs in a real git repo; NO neuter is claimed for it — post-D29 IgnoreSet::build probes each directory directly, so removing git init is expected to change nothing, and this is hygiene not a vacuity fix
unignore_is_honored_without_other_watched_activity runs under SingleDaemonGuard so a RED run (which TDD and every neuter check produce by design) cannot leak a live daemon

eviction_keeps_open_turn_blob: a blob cited only by open.json and one evictable old turn survives an over-budget enforce_budget pass (fixture mtime backdated so the A3(c) freshness guard cannot rescue it vacuously)
eviction_keeps_pinned_blob: a blob cited only by a memory.jsonl pin survives eviction and verify's pin-diff still renders afterwards

eviction_keeps_torn_line_refs: a blob cited ONLY by a torn line (truncated mid-JSON, valid sha256 inside) in log.jsonl, and separately in a truncated open.json, survives eviction — this is what lifts eviction to purge --orphans' torn-line guarantee

status_eviction_keeps_open_turn_blob: the CALL SITE is wired, not just the core fn — an integration-level status run on an over-budget store with an open turn keeps the blob, and passing an empty set at the call site reds this while the core unit test stays green

status_attributes_protected_bytes: over-budget status where every candidate is protected explains why 0 bytes were freed, naming pinned/in-flight, so the fix does not re-create the 'over budget, 0 freed' dishonest-status class

state_survives_one_bad_field: a state.json whose signal_offset is a string preserves every OTHER field (pid, snapshot_failures, io_failed) and leaves only signal_offset at default, incrementing a parse-failure counter — never the whole-struct unwrap_or_default reset
corrupt_field_does_not_replay_signal_inbox: a corrupt unrelated field (io_failed) must not reset signal_offset — seed 4096, assert still 4096, because a reset offset replays the entire signal inbox
a wholly unparseable state.json still yields defaults AND a non-zero parse-failure counter, and status says so — the unrecoverable case is counted, never silent
doctor_state_parse_advisory_never_flips_exit: doctor reports state-parse degradation, exits 0 and keeps ok true — doctor all-pass exit 0 is this repo's deploy gate and an advisory must not break it

status_reload_line_is_epoch_scoped: after a daemon restart the rendered ignore-reload figure restarts from zero while the lifetime total persists in state.json — answers open question 1 with option (a), reversing last round's default-by-omission

status_json_carries_degraded_fields: status --json on a DEGRADED store carries every field the text banner reports (snapshot_failures, prompt_put_failures, io_failed, state_parse_failures) — a monitoring script must never see LESS than the text surface
ack_degraded_json_is_not_prose: status --ack-degraded --json emits parseable JSON or exits non-zero with a clap conflict — it never prints prose to stdout under a --json flag
bare status output is unchanged for a healthy store — pinned because three renderers now read the same state

narrowing_mid_debounce_still_stages_pending_paths: pins the over-record mirror of the documented residual window — a path already in pending under the older wider rules is still staged at the next flush even if a mid-debounce .gitignore edit now ignores it. NO neuter is claimed: this pins existing behavior rather than proving a fix
the SECOND mutation of that same path after the narrowing rule lands is NOT recorded — this half does have a neuter (revert the rebuild-gate loop-tick move) and must go RED under it

no stale reload line across an epoch boundary: after a daemon restart with NO new rebuild yet, and while the daemon is stopped (pid 0), status renders no ignore-reload line at all — the previous epoch's count is never attributed to the current one
the README sentence 'the text line resets on each daemon restart' is literally true against the running binary, verified by observation not by rewording the claim to match the code

claim: status_omits_stale_epoch_reload_line pins the --json seam as well as the text seam: neutering ONLY status_json back to the raw epoch_ignore_rebuilds field must red this test by name, since status_report and status_json are independent readers and the gate proved a json-only neuter previously survived the whole suite

epoch identity is a nonce stamped at acquire_lock, not the pid: a new daemon epoch that happens to reuse the previous epoch's pid still renders zero reloads until its own first rebuild, and that rebuild does not accumulate onto the dead epoch's count

the nonce reset is symmetric across reader and writer: state::record_ignore_rebuild resets on nonce change and the render gate keys on the same nonce, so neither side can attribute a dead epoch's reloads to the live one
a state.json written by an older binary (no nonce field) still parses and degrades honestly rather than reporting a stale epoch count as current

the rebuild-rate bound is expressed platform-independently: the invariant is 'rebuilds are bounded by POLL ticks elapsed, never by raw event count', asserted so that it discriminates its per-event neuter on BOTH macOS/FSEvents (which coalesces) and Linux/inotify (which does not)

unignore_is_honored_without_other_watched_activity passes on Linux/inotify as well as macOS/FSEvents, and if its positive control cannot record there, the root cause is diagnosed and named rather than the deadline being widened until it goes green

admit_existing_contents fires only for events that genuinely materialize new content at a path — Create and rename-in — never for a metadata-only event on an existing directory; a touch or chmod on an existing dir stages NOTHING, so the daemon cannot fabricate op:modify entries or let them fold into a rich agent turn and be blamed on the agent

a metadata-only event on a directory that PRE-DATES the daemon stages nothing on macOS — the case the current test cannot see, because FSEvents delivers coalesced flag unions carrying historical ItemCreated and admitted_dirs is empty for every directory existing at daemon start

a directory renamed away and recreated is still admitted: IN_MOVED_FROM maps to Modify(Name(From)) not Remove(Folder), so the admitted_dirs entry must be cleared on any rename of that path or the original Linux event-loss class reopens for mv dir dir.bak && mkdir dir

SUPERSEDES clm_2FMT7QQ87Y, whose text claimed a platform-INDEPENDENT bound. That is not what shipped and the plan's premise was wrong: elapsed/POLL is unusable because recv_timeout returns immediately when a message is queued, so the loop ticks far faster than once per POLL during a burst. Measured correct-vs-neutered are macOS 3-4 vs 15-18 and Linux 13-21 vs 87-103 — Linux's correct ceiling EXCEEDS macOS's neutered floor, so one constant is mathematically impossible. Delivered is a cfg(target_os) split (1..=10 macOS, 1..=45 Linux), each side discriminating its own neuter

watcher_arm_stamp_keys_on_current_epoch_nonce: calling the real stamp_watcher_armed() sets watcher_armed_nonce equal to the CURRENT epoch_nonce, so a stale armed nonce carried over from a previous epoch does not read as armed

live_daemon_reports_watcher_armed: a real spawned daemon reaches watcher_armed_nonce == epoch_nonce in state.json within the wait bound, proving run() actually calls stamp_watcher_armed after .watch() succeeds — the call site is unreachable from a unit test

release_lock clears watcher_armed_nonce alongside epoch_nonce: acquire_lock_stamps_a_fresh_epoch_nonce_and_release_clears_it asserts the new field is cleared on clean stop, so a stopped daemon never leaves a value that reads as armed

The watcher-arm race class is closed at the population level: no live-daemon test can any longer observe an event emitted in the ~4.3ms window between the pid being written by acquire_lock and the watcher being armed. This is NOT directly assertable by any fixture — the mechanism tests are proxies only; the population claim is measured over CI history via a VERIFY-LEDGER row.
ci.yml gains workflow_dispatch WITHOUT regressing the existing triggers: push on branch main and pull_request both remain present and unchanged

rebuild_count_is_bounded_by_writes emits its observed rebuild count unconditionally, so a GREEN CI run carries the number in its log — previously the count surfaced only in the assert-failure message and cargo captures stdout on pass, making a green run evidence-free

The Linux leg runs on a real GitHub runner for this branch's HEAD, evidenced by a run URL with the test job green on the ubuntu matrix legs, and the observed rebuild_count from that runner is recorded in VERIFY-LEDGER.md. Not falsifiable by any local test — the criterion IS the run URL.

claim: AC3.1: Recorder::stage accumulates dedup_hits and dedup_reread_bytes on the snapshot path — same content staged twice increments hits by 1 and reread_bytes by the object length; a content change does not increment; an over-cap file does not increment. Driven directly against Recorder::stage with no live daemon and no hook, so persist-path put_result calls cannot inflate the counters
AC3.2: status --json exposes both dedup counters, and a state.json missing those fields renders 0 for both while preserving every sibling field (per-field parse, not struct-level reset)

AC3.3: the dedup heal path and the mtime-bump path assert the same behavior, and the heal test pins Decision 6's concrete values (deduped false, reread_bytes 0) — the corrupt-fallthrough re-read is a heal event, not steady-state dedup cost, and must not be mixed into the figure this round exists to get

AC3.4: Recorder::stage alone never writes state.json even when staging a batch containing dedup hits — the file is absent or byte-identical after staging, and changes only once drain_recorder_stats runs, bounding write cadence to at most one state.json write per flush rather than one per event

P3-F1: the symlink snapshot put inside Recorder::stage is counted by the dedup instrumentation like every other stage put — a repeated unchanged symlink increments dedup_hits and dedup_reread_bytes, closing the gap where store.put discarded deduped/reread_bytes; the source comment and README no longer claim the symlink put is excluded, since the plan's only two named exclusions are both prompt puts in persist/recover_orphan

P3-F2: the dedup counters are documented as epoch-scoped mirrors rather than lifetime totals — drain_recorder_stats assigns from a per-run Recorder, so after a daemon restart status renders the previous epoch's figure until the new epoch's first dedup hit; README states this explicitly so a monitoring script is not misled by a silently non-monotonic counter
